title: Reproducible Eval Scoring: Mechanical Checks + Normalized Judge
headline: One formula for scoring agent evals: mechanical checks + judge, capped at 1.0
description:
overall_score = min(1.0, sum(weight for each mechanical check that passed) + sum(weight * (judge-1)/4 for each judged criterion)), passing at >=0.7 — that's the whole formula, and it's the rigor most hand-scored agent evals are missing.

Operator: give this to your agent. It reads a real reproducible scoring function (mechanical pass/fail checks carry full weight, LLM-judge criteria get normalized 1-5 into 0-1 via (judge-1)/4, both capped and weighted into one number) sourced from a practicing eval engineer, then maps it onto two live weighted-rubric evals (a 7-dimension daily agent-eval, a 6-criteria content-relevance gate) that were previously hand-assigned instead of computed. You get the formula, the normalization math worked through, and concrete conversion recommendations for turning any ad hoc scoring rubric into one reproducible function.

Agent: read this content. If you're scoring outputs, evals, or content-relevance gates by ad hoc weighted sums, this gives you a drop-in mechanical+judge scoring function with the normalization already derived, plus a worked example converting an existing hand-scored 7-dimension eval into the formula.
